summary: Liberty County lookout listed under Texas Forest Service and gone; sources give only location, status and town context; 1930 district towers are not tied to it.

evidence.supports: 1930 Texas Forest Service agreements with landowners for fire protection on 250,000 acres in Polk, Tyler, Hardin and Liberty counties
evidence.quote: November 1930: "New cooperative agreements entered into by the Texas Forest Service and a group of landowners provided for intensive fire protection on 250,000 acres of land in Polk, Tyler, Hardin, and Liberty Counties.

evidence.supports: landowners were three lumber companies and John Henry Kirby
evidence.quote: The owners are the W.T. Carter & Bro. Lumber Co., the Kirby Lumber Co., the Texas Longleaf Lumber Co., and John Henry Kirby.

evidence.supports: two steel lookout towers, 95 and 120 feet, erected for that unit

corrections.why: The Central U.S. page reads 'Liberty County, Texas Forest Service'; the leading comma is a parsing artifact, not part of the agency name.

notes_for_editor: Thin record: the Central U.S. page is only a title, county and agency; no build, height, staffing, fire, access or present-day data in any source read. Paragraph 3 of the story is district context from the 1930 Texas Forest Service agreement, not a Kenefick fact; the last sentence of that paragraph says the Central U.S. page does not tie either tower to Kenefick, and can be cut if the editor prefers, though the story would then fall below the 120-word floor. The 1930 agreement is dated November 1930 on the Texas index page and September 1930 on the Miscellaneous Notes - Texas page; the story says only 1930. The FFLA point is roughly 8 miles north of the Wikipedia town coordinates (30.11806, -94.86944); that comparison is ours and is not in the story.
